newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zaire rebel leader expected in Zimbabwe - diplomats.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel leader expected in Zimbabwe - diplomats.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila is expected in Zimbabwe soon to seek President Robert Mugabe's support ahead of peace talks with his government foes, diplomatic sources said on Wednesday.
"He is likely to be here anytime soon," a diplomat told Reuters. Diplomats did not know his exact arrival time and government officials were unavailable for comment.
Diplomats said Mugabe's influence in the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) was key to Kabila's visit.

"President Mugabe is a big player on the African diplomatic stage. In June, he will be become the next chairman of the OAU and we understand -- and it makes sense -- that Kabila wants his ear," one diplomatic source said.

Kabila, who met South African President Nelson Mandela last month, was also likely to target other southern African leaders "for some understanding, if not support" for his campaign to topple Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, a source said.
Talks between Mobutu's representatives and Kabila's rebel movement will probably be held in South Africa on Saturday, led by United Nations and OAU negotiator Mohamed Sahnoun.
The rebels have been fighting Mobutu's forces since October and now control about a quarter of the country.
